key_insight: A single data-driven closure trained at the expected viscosity can be reused across random-viscosity realizations, with physical constraints improving reduced-order model accuracy and robustness.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a potentially lower-cost approach to uncertainty quantification for transient incompressible flows without training a separate closure for every viscosity realization.
method: Combine POD reduced-order models, spatial filtering, and stochastic collocation.
Learn a closure from the full-order solution at the expected viscosity and reuse it across realizations.
Impose physical constraints in CDDC-UQ-ROM to improve robustness.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D cylinder flow with a 5D random viscosity field at mean Re = 100 and 500 included varied correlation lengths, in- and out-of-sample settings, energy-moment errors, and reduced training data; CDDC-UQ-ROM was the most accurate and robust model tested.
watch_item: Reusing the expected-viscosity closure is an approximation; transferability beyond the tested flow and parameter regimes remains unestablished.
paper_title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
